sections.h2: Your three routes for removing an occupant
sections.html:
Arkansas offers owners a civil suit named unlawful detainer, a filing under the 2007 residential landlord-tenant statute, and a criminal complaint for refusing to leave. Owners usually pick one of the first two.

Unlawful detainer is defined in Ark. Code § 18-60-304. Holding over once the lease expires qualifies. So does ignoring a written demand to go, skipping rent and then staying put after a three-day written warning, letting the home turn unsafe or unhealthy, or permitting a common nuisance. This is the eviction type owners file most often.

The statutory route begins at § 18-17-901. An owner or agent can go to district court over unpaid rent, an expired occupancy term, or a broken rental agreement. For homes, five days of late rent after the due date works as legal notice that a filing may follow.

The warning an owner must give turns on the reason for ending occupancy. Pick the row that fits your facts and your lease, since the waits are not uniform.

SituationNotice or waiting periodStatute
Rent unpaid, unlawful detainerThree days' written notice to quit§ 18-60-304(3)
Rent unpaid, Landlord-Tenant ActTermination allowed once rent sits unpaid five days past due§ 18-17-701(b)
Other lease violationWritten notice setting an end date no sooner than 14 days after receipt, unless cured§ 18-17-701(a)
Week-to-week tenancyWritten notice at least 7 days ahead of the end date§ 18-17-704(a)
Month-to-month tenancyWritten notice at least 30 days ahead of the end date§ 18-17-704(b)
Criminal failure to vacateTen days' written notice to vacate§ 18-16-101(b)

Boiled down, civil waits start at three days for rent, 14 days for other breaches, and a month for month-to-month occupancy. An owner may also end a tenancy without stating a cause: one rental period of notice ends an oral lease, and a written lease sets its own notice.

A tenant who is still inside after the deadline leads the owner to file a complaint. Five stages follow.

  • Service. A process server or certified mail has to put the summons and complaint in the tenant's hands.
  • Five days to object. After receiving a summons, the tenant gets five days to file a written objection with the court clerk. Without one, the county sheriff may remove the tenant.
  • Order to vacate or show cause. When the complaint comes with a sworn statement from a person who knows the grounds, the court orders the tenant to leave or to come in and show cause, with ten calendar days running from service. Filing a written answer satisfies the appearance.
  • Hearing. Once the tenant appears, the judge listens to each side. If the tenant prevails, occupancy continues until it ends by agreement or law, rent lapses, or a later eviction case works (§ 18-17-908).
  • Writ of possession. A win for the owner means the clerk issues a writ and the sheriff serves it, which gives the tenant 24 hours to go. Enforcement follows § 18-60-310, as § 18-17-913 directs.

Treat each period as a floor. Hearing dates come from the court calendar, so nothing in the code promises a total timeline from first notice to move-out.

A tenant commits a misdemeanor by knowingly staying after receiving ten days' written notice from the owner, an agent or the owner's attorney. See Ark. Code § 18-16-101.

The section adds that a renter who misses rent gives up the right to remain in the dwelling. The fine on conviction runs from $1 to $25 per offense, and every day of deliberate holdover after the notice period ends is a fresh offense.

sections.h2: Can a landlord change the locks or shut off utilities?
sections.html:
No. Only a court order and a sheriff-executed writ of possession can put a tenant out.

  • Swapping the locks counts as a self-help eviction.
  • Hauling out belongings or removing doors and windows counts too.
  • Turning off water, power or other utilities counts as well.

There is one carve-out: those acts may be fine after the tenant has left, or when the owner has a reasonable belief the place is abandoned. A locked-out tenant may sue for forcible entry. The judge can order access restored and award damages, costs and fees. The owner may answer with a counterclaim to evict in the same suit, because a lockout does not create a right to stay where legal grounds for eviction exist.

Once a tenancy is over, by choice or by court order, anything left inside is considered abandoned, and the owner can deal with it however seems best with no claim by the tenant. Items remaining on site also secure a landlord's lien for amounts the tenant promised to pay.

When officers carry out the removal, goods the tenant cannot carry are moved and held at the tenant's cost. A tenant who leaves voluntarily and abandons things lets the owner discard or sell them.

sections.h2: Can a tenant withhold rent over repairs?
sections.html:
No, withholding is not allowed. Section 18-17-502 prevents a tenant from offsetting or holding back rent over a claimed or real shortfall in the implied quality standards. No part of the chapter excuses payment.

For leases signed or renewed after November 1, 2021, the law reads in a baseline: hot and cold running water, electricity, drinkable water, working sewer and plumbing, a sound roof and building envelope, and heating and cooling where the home came with them. A tenant whose unit falls short sends written notice. With rent current and no repair after 30 calendar days, the only remedy is leaving the lease penalty-free and recovering any deposit that can be recovered.

Little Rock layers on its own minimum standards for private rentals holding two or more dwellings. A watertight roof is one. Complaints go to the Department of Housing and Neighborhood Programs, 500 West Markham Street, Suite 120W, phone (501) 371-6825.

Under § 18-17-701(c), an owner may collect actual damages, ask for an injunction, and get a judgment or eviction order from circuit or district court with no bond.

Fees for the owner's lawyer are possible if the tenant's nonpayment lacks good faith, and for other willful violations. For a holdover, § 18-17-704 also allows fees where the holdover is in bad faith. A willful violation can add three months of periodic rent or double the actual damages, whichever is larger.

sections.h2: Eviction and selling a rented house
sections.html:
Selling and evicting are separate tracks. The code decides who may possess the house, and a sale does not end a tenancy by itself. Read the lease and speak with an attorney before telling any buyer the house will come vacant.

Some practical links exist. Non-renewal is allowed for any reason except those the Fair Housing Act forbids. Month-to-month tenants are owed 30 days' written notice. You can ask a cash buyer at the outset whether it will accept the house with the tenant in place, which skips the wait for a court date.

Gather these before listing a tenant-occupied house:

  • The lease, any renewal and each notice served.
  • A rent ledger showing paid and late months.
  • Court filings, so the title company can see how a case stands.

The deed brings its own paperwork. State transfer tax runs $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration when the deal exceeds $100, paid through a stamp on the deed. Let the assessor know when an owner-occupied home becomes a rental, since the homestead credit covers a principal residence only.

faqs.q: How long does an Arkansas eviction take?
faqs.a: No law gives a total. Notice ranges from three days to 30 days, the objection window is five days, a show-cause order allows up to ten days to appear, and a writ gives 24 hours. A contested case also waits on a hearing date.

faqs.q: Is eviction a crime in Arkansas?
faqs.a: Only failure to vacate is criminal. Section 18-16-101 makes it a misdemeanor to knowingly stay past a ten-day written notice, with a $1 to $25 fine per offense and a new offense each day.

faqs.q: Can a landlord evict without going to court?
faqs.a: No. A court order comes first and the sheriff executes the writ of possession. Lock changes, door or window removal and utility shutoffs are unlawful self-help unless the tenant is gone or the place seems abandoned.

faqs.q: Does a pending eviction stop me from selling the house?
faqs.a: Nothing bars a sale while a case is open. The lease and the buyer's terms decide the tenant's fate, so have an Arkansas attorney review any contract that promises vacant possession.

faqs.q: Where can a tenant find free legal help with an eviction?
faqs.a: Legal Aid of Arkansas helps qualifying tenants for free at 1-800-952-9243.
